raw_recipe.headline: The Best Marinade Around
raw_recipe.description: The best store bought marinade can't compare to this homemade one. Soy sauce, olive oil, lemon juice, and garlic come together for the best marinade around.
raw_recipe.name: The Best Marinade Around

review.reviewBody: 5 STARS IS A RIP OFF!!! This one truly deserves 10 stars! We just finished dinner and I couldn't wait to get my review in... This was incredible... Really! Absolutely incredible. I used some boneless, thick cut, pork chops which usually come out way too dry for my liking. (Especially when you do them on the grill.) Well, my hubby grilled them and we were OH SO delighted when we bit into that first bite. It was seriously the most moist chop I've ever had! HANDS DOWN!!! What I cannot believe is that just 4 simple ingredients make such a HUGE difference! The only change I made was to use "low sodium" soy sauce, and I marinated it for about 4 hours. These chops were OUTSTANDING!!! I think I'll be buying pork chops more often these days!!!

Surprised this marinade only rates 4 stars, it's probably the best 4 ingredient recipe I have seen and you probably have all the things you need in your fridge. For a quick little something to add flavor to your meat it is hard to beat this. I would absolutely say to use Low Sodium soy sauce though. Enjoy!
Very typical. Used less soy and added Worcestershire. I added a splash of rice vinegar for a little bite. I also tried it with red pepper flakes and that was good too.
Hands down best steak marinade I've ever made. I added about a tablespoon of Dijon mustard and let my sirloin tip steaks marinade about 8 hours. Spectacular!

This is a typical Islander marinade, we also add onions, garlic, seasoned salt and black pepper. I grew up eating with this marinade as my mom used lemon, lime or vinegar with a little water to tenderize the meat if the flavors are too strong. Beef ribs or steaks, pork ribs or chops, chicken pieces, venison such as deer or elk meat is used as well. A typical meal is shown with rice and finadeni, an islander salsa then a salad and the pork short ribs...

My grandfather taught me this marinade 35yrs ago. I’ve been using it ever since. It works great on both chicken and pork as well. The thicker the meat, the longer the soak. Full size bone in chicken breasts work best with an overnight soak. I find ziplock bags work best since all sides of the meat are in constant contact with the marinade. One other trick works wonders. Buy yourself a Jacquard hand held meat tenderizer. Run this through the meat before you marinate. The tiny piercings will allow the meat to soak up more marinade in less time.

Many Islanders marinade somewhat like this but I think the reason many say that it was too salty or tasted like soy sauce is because it only calls for 1 lemon and let's face it, not all lemons give the same amount of juice. So, I would taste the lemon and soy mix first before adding oil. It should be the perfect balance of sour/salty and not too sour and not too salty. Hope others will give it another go because it is simple yet delicious

This is the only marinade I use on steaks and the only change I make is to add freshly ground pepper.

Usually put the steaks (most often strip loin) and marinate in a ziplock in the morning and grill them for supper that evening. The steaks sear nicely and are juicy and tender. Delicious!
I made a double amount and put it in the crockpot to cook some beef for a stew and it was great..

Best Marinade All Around Haiku: "Way too much soy sauce, threw off balance with its salt. Reduce it by half." I made the recipe as written and marinated two small chicken breasts in it for 2 hrs., but found that after grilling, the soy sauce was just over-powering. If it was in the same ratio as the olive oil, I think it would've been better, or perhaps low-sodium instead of regular.

My Husbands go to marinade for many years except he always used lime juice instead of lemon. Lots of garlic & cracked pepper. Excellent on rib eyes & boneless skinless chicken thighs. I don’t believe he used any oil though. We definitely always had compliments.

MAAAN! This marinade worked like a charm! I used on a flank steak and my oh my it was delicious! The only tweak I made was to add a few dashes of Worcestershire sauce (because I love it!) I will definitely be using it again!
I added 1/4 cup of Honey and some Thyme.
I made this recipe last week for pork chops, and again today for sirloin steaks. It’s great! The instructions say it’s enough for one steak, but I found that it’s easily enough for 3 chops or steaks.

Renee Ridgeway - your passionate and heartfelt review is what inspired me to try this. Thank you! And I agree. For 4 little ingredients that most households have in their pantry- this is phenomenal. The second factor - which is made easier in todays age with timers and grill-safe digital thermometers- is that if you can cook to the correct temp, you will not be disappointed. Followed exactly and on thick pork chops. While no, this is not the most unique flavor profile, as written - and with a perfectly cooked chop - AMAZING! Keeping this recipe for those weekends when you want to impress without slaving in the kitchen! Thank you H Roberts!
Followed recipe exactly. This is a keeper. If some reviewers did not follow as directed, they need not give their reviews.
I have used this marinade on pork and chicken with a few tweaks. Easy recipe

I'm just seeing this recipe here, but I have used it for years! I usually use it on chicken breast, which is otherwise often more dry and bland than I prefer. I also use it on kabobs with chicken, onions, peppers and pineapple -- grilled pineapple with this marinade is amazing! I learned this marinade recipe from a friend over 40 years ago, so to say it is "a keeper" is an understatement!
